step1_figure.description: Figure 25.19 shows the simulation schematic of the fully differential sample-and-hold circuit using bottom-plate sampling with NMOS switches, 1 pF sampling and load capacitors, and a differential op-amp with CMFB.

common_mode_voltage.description: Output and input common-mode voltage around which differential signals swing

equation.explanation: The average of the op-amp outputs is set to VDD/2 to maximize dynamic range and symmetric output swing.
equation.assumptions: Symmetric power supply rails from ground to VDD.

sky130_expected.calculation: With VDD = 1.0 V (Baker simulation schematic) or VDD = 1.8 V (standard SKY130), VCM is nominal VDD/2. In the schematic, VCM source is fixed to 500 mV (0.5 V).
sky130_expected.reasoning: The common-mode reference VCM is established by VCM1 at 500 mV.

virtual_short_input_difference.description: Differential voltage between op-amp inputs during the sampling phase (phi1 closed)

equation.explanation: High open-loop gain and unity feedback during phi1 force the differential input voltage close to zero.
equation.assumptions: Op-amp gain AOL is very large (AOL = gm*Rout = 150u * 10M = 1500 V/V).

sky130_expected.calculation: A_OL = G1 * R1 = 150 uS * 10 MOhm = 1500 V/V. For a peak differential output swing of 200 mV, |vp - vm| = 200 mV / 1500 = 133 uV.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Finite transconductance and output resistance limit AOL to ~1500.

differential_output_swing.description: Maximum peak-to-peak differential output voltage swing

equation.explanation: Each single-ended output swings between 0 and VDD, so the maximum difference is VDD - 0 = VDD and minimum is 0 - VDD = -VDD, giving a total swing of 2*VDD.

sky130_expected.calculation: For VDD = 1.0 V, v_out,diff_pk-pk = 2 * 1.0 V = 2.0 V. For input sinusoidal peak of 200 mV differential, linear swing is 400 mV peak-to-peak.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Under test conditions, the input is 200 mV pk-pk differential, which should transfer 1:1 to output.

differential_voltage_gain.description: Differential voltage gain of the sample-and-hold in hold mode

equation.explanation: In hold mode, the op-amp operates as a follower holding the voltage sampled across the hold capacitor, yielding unity gain.
equation.assumptions: Op-amp gain is large, bottom plate parasitic Cp is driven by low impedance, and top plate parasitic is small.

sky130_expected.reasoning: Finite AOL and switch charge sharing cause slight gain loss.

differential_offset_error.description: Differential offset voltage caused by clock feedthrough and charge injection

equation.explanation: Because bottom plate sampling turns off phi1 switches first while inputs are at VCM, charge injection is signal-independent and matched on both sides, canceling as common-mode.
equation.assumptions: Switch sizing and layout capacitance are perfectly matched.

sky130_expected.calculation: Switch matching is symmetric in the schematic. Residual differential offset arises only from slight mismatch in input dynamics, expected < 1 mV.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Bottom-plate sampling provides first-order cancellation of charge injection.

hold_mode_settling_time.description: Time required for the differential output to settle to within 1% of final value after phi3 turns on

equation.explanation: Switch on-resistance and hold/load capacitance set the RC settling time constant tau = Ron * CH.
equation.assumptions: Op-amp slewing does not dominate and switch Ron governs settling.

sky130_expected.calculation: NMOS W/L = 10u/1u. Ron = 1 / (un*Cox * (W/L) * (VGS - Vth)) = 1 / (270u * 10 * (1.8 - 0.5 - 0.42)) = 421 Ohm. Tau = Ron * C_H = 421 * 1pF = 0.42 ns. Settling to 1% is ~5*tau = 2.1 ns.
sky130_expected.reasoning: On-resistance of 10u/1u NMOS switches with 1 pF load charges within a few nanoseconds.

step3_testbench.description: Transient testbench for the fully-differential sample-and-hold circuit verifying tracking gain, common-mode level, differential swing, virtual ground offset, and settling.
step3_testbench.spice:
* Fully-Differential Sample-and-Hold Testbench
.lib "${SKY130_PDK}" tt

* Parameter definitions for switches (detail from Fig. 25.19: 10/1)
.param W_xm1=10u L_xm1=1u
.param W_xm2=10u L_xm2=1u
.param W_xm3=10u L_xm3=1u
.param W_xm4=10u L_xm4=1u
.param W_xm5=10u L_xm5=1u
.param W_xm6=10u L_xm6=1u
.param W_xm7=10u L_xm7=1u
.param W_xm8=10u L_xm8=1u

* DUT Netlist
V1 Vinm 0 SINE(500m -100m 5MEG)
V2 Vinp 0 SINE(500m 100m 5MEG)
C1 vm N001 1e-12
C2 vp N003 1e-12
C3 voutp 0 1e-12
C4 voutm 0 1e-12
xm1 N001 phi2 vinp 0 sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 w={W_xm1} l={L_xm1}
xm2 N003 phi2 vinm 0 sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 w={W_xm2} l={L_xm2}
xm3 vop phi1 vm 0 sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 w={W_xm3} l={L_xm3}
xm4 vom phi1 vp 0 sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 w={W_xm4} l={L_xm4}
xm5 vop phi3 N001 0 sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 w={W_xm5} l={L_xm5}
xm6 N003 phi3 vom 0 sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 w={W_xm6} l={L_xm6}
xm7 voutp phi3 vop 0 sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 w={W_xm7} l={L_xm7}
xm8 vom phi3 voutm 0 sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 w={W_xm8} l={L_xm8}
G1 0 vop vp vm 150u
G2 vom 0 vp vm 150u
R1 vop N002 10000000.0
R2 N002 vom 10000000.0
G3 0 vop VCM N002 10u
G4 0 vom VCM N002 10u
VCM1 VCM 0 500m

* Clock Generation: 50 MHz (Period = 20ns)
* phi1 turns off first (bottom plate sampling), then phi2, then non-overlapping phi3
Vphi1 phi1 0 PULSE(0 1.8 0 0.2n 0.2n 5n 20n)
Vphi2 phi2 0 PULSE(0 1.8 0 0.2n 0.2n 7n 20n)
Vphi3 phi3 0 PULSE(0 1.8 10n 0.2n 0.2n 8n 20n)

* Simulation Control
.control
tran 0.05n 200n

* Derived signals
let vin_diff = v(vinp) - v(vinm)
let vout_diff = v(voutp) - v(voutm)
let vcm_out = 0.5 * (v(vop) + v(vom))
let v_vshort = v(vp) - v(vm)

* Measurements
meas tran vcm_avg avg vcm_out from=10n to=200n
meas tran vin_diff_max max vin_diff from=50n to=200n
meas tran vin_diff_min min vin_diff from=50n to=200n
meas tran vout_diff_max max vout_diff from=50n to=200n
meas tran vout_diff_min min vout_diff from=50n to=200n

let diff_swing = vout_diff_max - vout_diff_min
let in_swing = vin_diff_max - vin_diff_min
let diff_gain = diff_swing / in_swing
let diff_offset = (vout_diff_max + vout_diff_min) / 2

meas tran max_vshort max abs(v_vshort) from=1n to=5n

print vcm_avg
print diff_swing
print diff_gain
print diff_offset
print max_vshort

quit
.endc
.end
